scoreExplanations.shapeVolume: The flat wedge cap and coarse source hair have become rounded, coherent volumes. Collar, cuffs, apron straps/pocket/tie and back knot add useful construction. The native cap fold is simpler than the target but reads as an intentional soft beret at the fixed scale.
scoreExplanations.color: Noor retains mediumtan/amber skin, green beret, blueblack hair, ivory coat, plum apron/tie and dark shoes. Warm muted rendering remains within her identity palette with clear large color blocks.
scoreExplanations.lightingHighlights: Broad soft lighting shows cap/hair/face volume in all four facings. Highlights are controlled and the ivory coat holds midtones. The result is quieter and less luminous than the imagegen target, while satisfying the symmetric world-sprite treatment.
scoreExplanations.materialDetail: Native construction carries the improvement: rounded hair locks, cap band/seam, cloth collars/cuffs and restrained plum details. There is no dependency on target micro-grain or painted body detail.
scoreExplanations.artifactFreeReadability: All required frames remain readable at logical scale with clean transparency, stable surfaces and source-consistent action/prop visibility. No material edge defect, new clipping, detached part, flicker or directional ground shadow was found.

observations.evidence: S idle and work show a broad rounded green crown with a curved folded seam, separate soft band and small top tab. E/W preserve the sloped/slouched identity; N retains coherent crown/band construction. The source angular wedge and abrupt face planes are removed without an oversized capture.

The blueblack fringe has clearly separated soft locks, the side opening keeps the ear and face profile visible, and N has rounded nape/back volume with readable broad highlights. Eyes, cheeks, nose and the gentler smile remain legible at logical size.

The ivory coat has shaped collar edges and rolled sleeve cuffs; plum straps, tie, pocket welt, apron hem and back bow/knot improve the chef role and garment hierarchy. Small contact-preserving shoes remain clear on light/gray, and the dark palette remains restrained on the dark composite.

The required green/blueblack/mediumtan/ivory/plum family is intact. Smooth broad gradients give the chosen warm-soft cartoon effect without a horizontal preferred key, target halo, blown coat or near-black rear dead spot.

All192 frames retain the authored planted stance and small idle/work/hold motion. Work displays the native knife only. Hold/load display the original2D dish, and load reaches out and back while ending held. No new one-way belt transfer was inferred from the state name. E/S/W dish readability and N occlusion remain consistent with the original attachment arrangement.

All48 light/gray/dark sheets and enlarged edge figures show clean alpha and stable rounded surfaces across all facings/states. No frame crop, halo, colored fringe, opaque card around the body, geometry pop, new cast shadow or garment self-intersection was found at the reviewed native/use scales.

remainingDifferences: The native beret uses a broad smooth crown and a restrained folded seam rather than the target’s deeper overlapping fabric fold. It preserves the role, palette and functional envelope and is accepted.
The native treatment is more matte and muted than the target’s glossy, golden imagegen rendering; target grain, bright rim halo and enlarged framing are intentionally absent.
Body/head proportions and the very small exposed dark shoes remain governed by native camera, rig, nominal height and contact requirements rather than the target’s enlarged front silhouette.

The inherited separate2D salmon dish overlaps the lower face in front/profile views and is mostly occluded in N. Exact native attachment/action behavior is preserved; a new release or belt-load trajectory is outside this candidate.
